raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

For hybrid SWA models such as DeepSeek-V4 served with the Mooncake unified-cache external linker, **cap SWA windows per radix path** with a new `--swa-max-states-per-path`, the SWA counterpart of `--mamba-max-states-per-path`. Every prefill chunk boundary leaves a live sliding window in the radix tree, and the linker persists all of them on write-through, so most stored SWA bytes are never matched again. With the cap, the shallowest interior windows beyond it are tombstoned after each insert (tail, fork, locked and pending-write nodes are kept; full KV is untouched), so the external store receives only the surviving windows. It reuses the Mamba per-path cap walk and runs on the Python TreeCore, which a positive cap selects through the existing Rust fallback policy. Default `-1` is unchanged.

## Validation

- pre-commit passes; the mem_cache unit suites pass, plus new tests for the SWA window cap.
- DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GB300, prefill 8x DEP8 / decode 4x DEP16, Mooncake external cache, agentic trace replay at concurrency 1920, a cap of 1 on prefill:

| | total tok/s/GPU | Mooncake bytes / key | evictions | prefix hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 123,012 / 123,061 | 0.64 MB | 10.5M | 95.2% |
| this PR | 130,044 / 128,832 / 130,835 (+5.8%) | 0.43 MB | 7.1M | 95.8% |

These runs also carried a Mooncake load-reservation change that has since been split out of this PR; it does not touch which windows are written.

## History

An earlier revision retained sparse SWA checkpoints by rewriting the linker's offload path (checkpoint range selection, mid-prefill checkpoint writes, supplementary window writes, replay-boundary plumbing). It measured best, 131,354 tok/s/GPU (+6.8%) on the same setup, but touched 11 files and only worked on the Python TreeCore, so it is reverted in this PR in favour of the per-path cap above, which keeps most of the gain with a fraction of the code. The revision before that bundled six changes; ablation on this workload showed no measurable gain from per-request chunk caps, deferred partial transfers, pipelined lookups or batched puts, so they were dropped. Decode capacity moved to #40153 and batched puts remain in #39696.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

The speed table does not isolate this PR. The description says the "this PR" runs "also carried a Mooncake load-reservation change that has since been split out", and the head commit message gives other numbers (129.4K, +5.2%). The description also has no launch or benchmark commands and no accuracy result.

**Fix**

Please add to the description:
- cap-only before/after throughput on the same GB300 setup (any commit of this PR is fine);
- the exact prefill, decode, and router launch commands, including `--swa-max-states-per-path 1` and the Mooncake linker flags, plus the trace-replay benchmark command and where the trace comes from;
- one accuracy result, such as GSM8K, with `--swa-max-states-per-path 1`, because the cap changes which SWA windows prefix matching reuses.

---

[by Claude Code] **Severity: nit | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

The title still says "and reserve Mooncake loads", but the description says the load-reservation change was split out. A squash merge would put the wrong summary into `main`.

**Fix**

Rename the PR, for example to "[Performance] Cap SWA windows per radix path with --swa-max-states-per-path".

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

The cap counts SWA nodes, not windows. A tail shorter than `sliding_window_size` needs SWA from its parent. If the inserting request has no lock on that parent, this walk tombstones it. The tail's window is then incomplete, so `match_prefix` cannot stop anywhere on the path.

**Example**

CPU run, page_size=1, window=4, cap=1: insert [0, 12) (evicted seqlen 8), then insert [0, 14) (evicted seqlen 10) with no lock, as when both requests run in one batch. `match_prefix([0, 14))` returns 0 tokens. With cap=-1 it returns 14. DeepSeek-V4 is not affected because its 256-token page covers a window.

**Fix**

Skip nodes within `sliding_window_size` tokens of the tail in this walk, and add this case as a test.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

These tests build `SWAComponent` with `object.__new__` on a fake tree core whose `_cascade_evict` does nothing. They reach only the shared `_evict_path_states_beyond_cap` walk. `test_cap_is_soft_for_fork_and_locked_nodes` and `test_negative_one_disables_cap` repeat the Mamba tests of that walk. No test covers the SWA-only code: the `EvictExcessPathStates` queued in `commit_insert_component_data`, `SWAComponent.apply_component_action`, the Python TreeCore fallback, or the `--swa-max-states-per-path` validation.

**Fix**

Replace the two repeated tests with one `build_fixture(CacheConfig(components=(FULL, SWA), sliding_window_size=4))` test, registered like `TestMambaPathCapWriteThroughOrdering`. Insert two chunks with cap 1. Check that the shallow window is a tombstone, full KV stays, `sanity_check()` passes, and the tail still matches. Add one `_rust_fallback_reason` case.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: nit | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

This comment says SWA shares the Mamba per-path cap. The next line reads the separate `--swa-max-states-per-path` flag; only the walk in `TreeComponent._evict_path_states_beyond_cap` is shared. A reader may think `--mamba-max-states-per-path` also limits SWA windows.

**Fix**

Drop the comment, or write `# Own flag; the trim walk is shared with Mamba.`
[by Claude Code] Follow-up review of 282fa68a47fae0cbb18e42e4ab954f4ee7a3e7e4. See the inline comments.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`RustUnifiedTreeCore.__init__` now calls `get_schedule()` for every tree with SWA. Code that builds a Rust SWA core without a published `schedule` namespace now fails with `ValueError: config namespace 'schedule' not published`.

**Example**

`test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` (CPU suite) builds SWA cores through `_swa_tree_core` without server args. Run as one file, as CI does, 6 tests fail, for example `test_configuration_reads_the_locked_rust_state` and `test_empty_match_result_is_root_anchored[True]`. With this `get_schedule()` read stubbed, they pass.

**Fix**

Add `swa_max_states_per_path` to `CacheInitParams` (default -1) and read it here and in `SWAComponent.__init__`, like `sliding_window_size`. Or publish server args in the test's `_tree_core` helper.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

This file is registered only for the CPU suite. `_build` calls `build_fixture`, which calls `get_device()`. On the CPU runner, which has no GPU and does not set `SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1`, `get_device()` raises `RuntimeError: No accelerator ...`. So the 4 tests in `TestSWAPathCapPythonTreeCore` and `TestSWAPathCapRustTreeCore` fail in `base-a-test-cpu`, and they never run on a GPU.

**Example**

On a CPU-only machine, `pytest test_swa_path_window_cap.py` gives 4 failed, 2 passed. With `get_device` patched to return `"cpu"`, all 6 pass on both TreeCores.

**Fix**

Follow `test_mamba_path_state_cap.py`: add `register_cuda_ci(...)`, and put `@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), ...)` on the two fixture classes.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This guard keeps nodes within `sliding_window_size` tokens of the tail end. The scheduler matches at most `input_len - 1` tokens, page-aligned down, so an exact repeat of a cached input stops one page before the tail end. That match needs SWA from `sliding_window_size + page_size` tokens back. The cap can tombstone it, so the repeat matches 0 tokens.

**Example**

page_size=1, window=4, cap=1: insert [0, 10) with evicted seqlen 4, then match [0, 9). Both TreeCores return 0 tokens; cap=-1 returns 9. page_size=4, window=2 fails the same way for a page-aligned input. Parallel sampling (n > 1) sends such repeats.

**Fix**

Protect `sliding_window_size + page_size` tokens (the span `_inc_session_coverage` uses) here and in `swa.rs`, and add this case as a test.

+"""Unit tests for the per-path SWA window cap."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci, register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+import unittest
+from array import array
+from collections import defaultdict
+
+import torch
+from test_unified_radix_cache_unittest import (
+    CacheConfig,
+    UnifiedRadixCacheSuite,
+    build_fixture,
+)
+
+from sglang.srt.arg_groups.kv_cache_hook import handle_cache_compatibility
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import InsertParams, MatchPrefixParams
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixKey
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.components.base import ComponentType
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.components.swa import SWAComponent
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.unified_tree_core import UnifiedTreeCore
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_radix_cache import UnifiedLRUList, UnifiedTreeNode
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+class _FakeTreeCore:
+    tree_components = (ComponentType.FULL, ComponentType.SWA)
+    page_size = 1
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.root_node = UnifiedTreeNode(self.tree_components)
+        self.evictable_device_leaves = set()
+        self.component_evictable_size_ = {ComponentType.SWA: 0}
+        self.component_protected_size_ = {ComponentType.SWA: 0}
+        self.lru_lists = {
+            ComponentType.SWA: UnifiedLRUList(ComponentType.SWA, self.tree_components)
+        }
+        self.host_lru_lists = {
+            ComponentType.SWA: UnifiedLRUList(
+                ComponentType.SWA, self.tree_components, use_host_ptr=True
+            )
+        }
+        self.evicted = []
+        self._is_tracking_unbacked_tokens = False
+        self._tracked_unbacked_tokens = 0
+
+    def _evict_component_and_detach_lru(self, node, component, *args, **kwargs):
+        self.evicted.append(node)
+        return UnifiedTreeCore._evict_component_and_detach_lru(
+            self, node, component, *args, **kwargs
+        )
+
+    def _cascade_evict(self, node, component, tracker, device_frees, host_frees):
+        pass
+
+
+class _FakeUnifiedCache:
+    tree_components = _FakeTreeCore.tree_components
+
+
+def _build_chain(cap, length=4):
+    core = _FakeTreeCore()
+    component = object.__new__(SWAComponent)
+    component.cache = _FakeUnifiedCache()
+    component.tree_core = core
+    component.swa_max_states_per_path = cap
+    component.sliding_window_size = 1
+
+    nodes = []
+    parent = core.root_node
+    for index in range(length):
+        node = UnifiedTreeNode(core.tree_components)
+        node.parent = parent
+        node.key = RadixKey(array("q", [index]))
+        node.component_data[ComponentType.FULL].value = torch.tensor([100 + index])
+        node.component_data[ComponentType.SWA].value = torch.tensor([index])
+        parent.children[index] = node
+        core.component_evictable_size_[ComponentType.SWA] += 1
+        core.lru_lists[ComponentType.SWA].insert_mru(node)
+        nodes.append(node)
+        parent = node
+    return component, nodes, core
+
+
+def _trim(component, tail):
+    device_frees = defaultdict(list)
+    component._evict_excess_path_states(tail, device_frees, defaultdict(list))
+    return device_frees
+
+
+class TestSWAPathWindowCap(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_server_arg_rejects_zero_and_values_below_negative_one(self):
+        for value in (0, -2):
+            args = ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", swa_max_states_per_path=value)
+            with (
+                self.subTest(value=value),
+                self.assertRaisesRegex(
+                    ValueError, "must be -1 \\(unlimited\\) or a positive integer"
+                ),
+            ):
+                handle_cache_compatibility(args)
+
+    def test_removes_shallow_windows_but_keeps_full_kv(self):
+        component, nodes, core = _build_chain(cap=1)
+
+        device_frees = _trim(component, nodes[-1])
+
+        self.assertEqual(core.evicted, [nodes[0], nodes[1]])
+        swa = [node.component_data[ComponentType.SWA].value for node in nodes]
+        self.assertEqual([value is None for value in swa], [True, True, False, False])
+        # SWA slots are freed through their FULL indices, never the SWA ones.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [value.item() for value in device_frees[ComponentType.SWA]], [100, 101]
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            all(
+                node.component_data[ComponentType.FULL].value is not None
+                for node in nodes
+            )
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(core.component_evictable_size_[ComponentType.SWA], 2)
+
+
+class _SWAPathCapFixtureBase:
+    cfg = CacheConfig(
+        components=(ComponentType.FULL, ComponentType.SWA), sliding_window_size=4
+    )
+    tree_core_backend: str
+    _rid = 0
+    _alloc = UnifiedRadixCacheSuite._alloc
+    _init_hicache = UnifiedRadixCacheSuite._init_hicache
+
+    def _build(self, cap):
+        return build_fixture(
+            self.cfg,
+            tree_core_backend=self.tree_core_backend,
+            swa_max_states_per_path=cap,
+        )
+
+    def _insert(self, cache, allocator, tokens, swa_evicted_seqlen):
+        value = self._alloc(allocator, len(tokens))
+        cache.insert(
+            InsertParams(
+                key=RadixKey(array("q", tokens)),
+                value=value[: len(tokens)],
+                component_evicted_seqlens={ComponentType.SWA: swa_evicted_seqlen},
+            )
+        )
+
+    def _match_len(self, cache, tokens):
+        match = cache.match_prefix(MatchPrefixParams(key=RadixKey(array("q", tokens))))
+        return len(match.device_indices), match.full_kv_hit_length
+
+    def test_trims_shallow_window_but_keeps_full_kv_and_tail_match(self):
+        cache, allocator, _ = self._build(cap=1)
+        tokens = list(range(16))
+
+        self._insert(cache, allocator, tokens[:8], swa_evicted_seqlen=4)
+        self._insert(cache, allocator, tokens, swa_evicted_seqlen=12)
+
+        # The first chunk's window is a tombstone; its full KV stays.
+        self.assertEqual(self._match_len(cache, tokens[:8]), (0, 8))
+        self.assertEqual(self._match_len(cache, tokens), (16, 16))
+        cache.sanity_check()
+
+    def test_keeps_parent_window_completing_a_short_tail(self):
+        """A tail shorter than the window keeps the parent window it needs,
+        even when no request locks that parent."""
+        cache, allocator, _ = self._build(cap=1)
+        tokens = list(range(14))
+
+        self._insert(cache, allocator, tokens[:12], swa_evicted_seqlen=8)
+        self._insert(cache, allocator, tokens, swa_evicted_seqlen=10)
+
+        self.assertEqual(self._match_len(cache, tokens), (14, 14))
+        cache.sanity_check()
+
+    def test_keeps_window_for_a_repeat_of_the_cached_input(self):
+        """A repeated input matches up to one page short of the cached tail;
+        the window ending there must survive the cap."""
+        cache, allocator, _ = self._build(cap=1)
+        tokens = list(range(10))
+
+        self._insert(cache, allocator, tokens, swa_evicted_seqlen=4)
+
+        self.assertEqual(self._match_len(cache, tokens[:-1]), (9, 9))
+        cache.sanity_check()
+
+    def test_write_through_backup_chain_survives_path_cap(self):
+        """Windows trimmed by the cap must not break a pending write-through
+        backup of their ancestors."""
+        cache, allocator, _ = self._build(cap=1)
+        self._init_hicache(cache)
+        cache.write_through_threshold = 2
+        tokens = list(range(24))
+
+        for end in (8, 16, 24, 24):
+            self._insert(cache, allocator, tokens[:end], swa_evicted_seqlen=0)
+        cache.writing_check(write_back=True)
+
+        self.assertEqual(self._match_len(cache, tokens[:-1]), (23, 23))
+        cache.sanity_check()
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "SWA pool fixtures need CUDA")
+class TestSWAPathCapPythonTreeCore(_SWAPathCapFixtureBase, CustomTestCase):
+    tree_core_backend = "python"
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "SWA pool fixtures need CUDA")
+class TestSWAPathCapRustTreeCore(_SWAPathCapFixtureBase, CustomTestCase):
+    tree_core_backend = "rust"
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

The cap counts SWA nodes, not windows. A tail shorter than `sliding_window_size` needs SWA from its parent. If the inserting request has no lock on that parent, this walk tombstones it. The tail's window is then incomplete, so `match_prefix` cannot stop anywhere on the path.

**Example**

CPU run, page_size=1, window=4, cap=1: insert [0, 12) (evicted seqlen 8), then insert [0, 14) (evicted seqlen 10) with no lock, as when both requests run in one batch. `match_prefix([0, 14))` returns 0 tokens. With cap=-1 it returns 14. DeepSeek-V4 is not affected because its 256-token page covers a window.

**Fix**

Skip nodes within `sliding_window_size` tokens of the tail in this walk, and add this case as a test.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

These tests build `SWAComponent` with `object.__new__` on a fake tree core whose `_cascade_evict` does nothing. They reach only the shared `_evict_path_states_beyond_cap` walk. `test_cap_is_soft_for_fork_and_locked_nodes` and `test_negative_one_disables_cap` repeat the Mamba tests of that walk. No test covers the SWA-only code: the `EvictExcessPathStates` queued in `commit_insert_component_data`, `SWAComponent.apply_component_action`, the Python TreeCore fallback, or the `--swa-max-states-per-path` validation.

**Fix**

Replace the two repeated tests with one `build_fixture(CacheConfig(components=(FULL, SWA), sliding_window_size=4))` test, registered like `TestMambaPathCapWriteThroughOrdering`. Insert two chunks with cap 1. Check that the shallow window is a tombstone, full KV stays, `sanity_check()` passes, and the tail still matches. Add one `_rust_fallback_reason` case.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: nit | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

This comment says SWA shares the Mamba per-path cap. The next line reads the separate `--swa-max-states-per-path` flag; only the walk in `TreeComponent._evict_path_states_beyond_cap` is shared. A reader may think `--mamba-max-states-per-path` also limits SWA windows.

**Fix**

Drop the comment, or write `# Own flag; the trim walk is shared with Mamba.`

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`RustUnifiedTreeCore.__init__` now calls `get_schedule()` for every tree with SWA. Code that builds a Rust SWA core without a published `schedule` namespace now fails with `ValueError: config namespace 'schedule' not published`.

**Example**

`test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` (CPU suite) builds SWA cores through `_swa_tree_core` without server args. Run as one file, as CI does, 6 tests fail, for example `test_configuration_reads_the_locked_rust_state` and `test_empty_match_result_is_root_anchored[True]`. With this `get_schedule()` read stubbed, they pass.

**Fix**

Add `swa_max_states_per_path` to `CacheInitParams` (default -1) and read it here and in `SWAComponent.__init__`, like `sliding_window_size`. Or publish server args in the test's `_tree_core` helper.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

This file is registered only for the CPU suite. `_build` calls `build_fixture`, which calls `get_device()`. On the CPU runner, which has no GPU and does not set `SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1`, `get_device()` raises `RuntimeError: No accelerator ...`. So the 4 tests in `TestSWAPathCapPythonTreeCore` and `TestSWAPathCapRustTreeCore` fail in `base-a-test-cpu`, and they never run on a GPU.

**Example**

On a CPU-only machine, `pytest test_swa_path_window_cap.py` gives 4 failed, 2 passed. With `get_device` patched to return `"cpu"`, all 6 pass on both TreeCores.

**Fix**

Follow `test_mamba_path_state_cap.py`: add `register_cuda_ci(...)`, and put `@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), ...)` on the two fixture classes.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This guard keeps nodes within `sliding_window_size` tokens of the tail end. The scheduler matches at most `input_len - 1` tokens, page-aligned down, so an exact repeat of a cached input stops one page before the tail end. That match needs SWA from `sliding_window_size + page_size` tokens back. The cap can tombstone it, so the repeat matches 0 tokens.

**Example**

page_size=1, window=4, cap=1: insert [0, 10) with evicted seqlen 4, then match [0, 9). Both TreeCores return 0 tokens; cap=-1 returns 9. page_size=4, window=2 fails the same way for a page-aligned input. Parallel sampling (n > 1) sends such repeats.

**Fix**

Protect `sliding_window_size + page_size` tokens (the span `_inc_session_coverage` uses) here and in `swa.rs`, and add this case as a test.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

The speed table does not isolate this PR. The description says the "this PR" runs "also carried a Mooncake load-reservation change that has since been split out", and the head commit message gives other numbers (129.4K, +5.2%). The description also has no launch or benchmark commands and no accuracy result.

**Fix**

Please add to the description:
- cap-only before/after throughput on the same GB300 setup (any commit of this PR is fine);
- the exact prefill, decode, and router launch commands, including `--swa-max-states-per-path 1` and the Mooncake linker flags, plus the trace-replay benchmark command and where the trace comes from;
- one accuracy result, such as GSM8K, with `--swa-max-states-per-path 1`, because the cap changes which SWA windows prefix matching reuses.
